decision: Multi-tenant Agora embedding is built on Metabase's native EE Tenants feature plus the native JWT SSO provider (no custom tenant model). Agora signs a JWT with jwt-shared-secret carrying the @tenant claim; /api/agora/embed/* accept it as `jwt`, verify it through auth-identity :provider/jwt, provision tenant + tenant user, auto-create a tenant group named after the tenant slug, create a :full-app-embed session and scope the dashboard list to the tenant collection tree (shared tenant collections excluded from static embeds). Legacy single-viewer mode (MB_AGORA_VIEWER_EMAIL, no jwt) is kept. /api/agora is wrapped in +message-only-exceptions. docker-compose default MB_EDITION is now ee.
rationale: Native Tenants already provide per-tenant collections, tenant groups with blocked-by-default data perms, tenant attributes for routing/sandboxing and an admin UI; reimplementing that would duplicate and diverge. Reusing :provider/jwt gives verified token handling, provisioning and tenant validations for free. Alternatives discarded: unauthenticated ?tenant= param (any caller could pick a tenant), a bespoke MB_AGORA_SHARED_SECRET (second secret with no added value over jwt-shared-secret), one-group-per-tenant done manually by admins (not turnkey), keeping +public-exceptions (Agora cannot distinguish expired token vs misconfiguration; /api/embed already uses message-only). Static embeds run without a user so shared-collection dashboards would bypass tenant data perms.
